tasks.title: Plain JSON validates within 10% of the baseline while own-data protections hold
tasks.spec: ## Repository: contract, all Files, Behavior, Checks and Completion evidence; Required behavior 1-5; Counterexamples 1-12 and their R-main/R-walk/Guard labels; CPU statistic; Security impact; Rollout order. Implement the schema-compiled walk and ownValue top-level element read together with their tests. Preserve the copy path, error texts, identity, exports, schemas, WIRE_VERSION and runtime dependency. The walk caches only by schema, never by input; unwraps the four wrappers; certifies object, dense array, record and single-object union branches exactly as specified; falls back for ambiguous object unions, lazy object/function values and enumerable Object.prototype keys. It runs no getters and makes no per-value allocation except the two permitted record key arrays. Keep helpers private and cognitive complexity at most 15. Replace only the named descriptor/get Proxy test with boolean-ok/no-throw assertions; keep hostile-trap tests. Add the standalone CPU script with unknown narrowing, document own-data elements and Proxy scope, bump to 1.7.1, and regenerate dist. README.md and test/validate.bench.test.ts are conditional paths: change only under the Files list's stated conditions. If both fixes already exist, follow the section's hold instruction. All TDD runs, performance runs and PR evidence belong to this single task; no compose check applies to this library.

acceptance.expected: 1.4.0, matching the spec's pinned runtime on every benchmark side. Record the version in the PR.
exit 0 on the candidate and each benchmark worktree; retain zod 4.6.7 and the existing tooling pins.

TDD evidence before source changes on 7ce23aaf3fa3e038f65ecfed755188b83bde143f: counterexamples 1 and 2 (R-main) fail because inherited top-level elements are accepted. Cases 3, 4 and 9 (R-walk) and guards 5-8, 10-12 pass. Record the failing test names and passing guards in the PR. Judge test results separately from this focused run's coverage threshold.

TDD evidence with only the spec-defined throwaway historical walk installed into 7ce23aaf3fa3e038f65ecfed755188b83bde143f and arrayProblem unchanged: counterexamples 1, 2, 3, 4 and 9 fail; guards 5-8, 10-12 pass. Record failing test names in the PR and revert the throwaway implementation before implementing the fix. No historical-walk change is committed. Coverage is not the red-test oracle.

exit 0 on the candidate: lint, build, typecheck and the full test suite pass, with line coverage at least 0.8 and cognitive complexity at most 15. Counterexamples 1-12 pass with their literal spec errors; getter counts stay 0 and successful values retain input identity. Existing token, audit, admin, hostile-proxy and dist smoke tests pass, including frozen arrays, array subclasses, null-prototype inputs and polluted Object/Array prototypes from the security checklist. The standalone CPU script is linted and typechecked but is not discovered as a test. Include check output, the added/changed test list and the applicable input-validation, accessor and secret-free-error security checklist results in the PR.

The only removed or weakened existing assertions belong to 'a Proxy whose get differs from its own data descriptor is judged by the descriptor'. Its replacement checks each existing validator call returns typeof result.ok === 'boolean' without throwing. Name this replacement in the PR. All other own-data and hostile-trap assertions remain. Counterexamples 1-12 use exported validators and the literal expectations from the spec.
